The update file is a nested squashfs: an inner xz rootfs.squashfs plus a MANIFEST, GPG-signed only 'if enabled' (SIGNING_KEY and SIGNING_PASSWORD set), wrapped in an outer squashfs so the updater can read the MANIFEST without extracting; a sha256 of the outer file is written beside it

In the 25.10.8 update client, integrity checks are checksums only: the download is compared to a sha256 from a manifest fetched over HTTPS from update.truenas.com, and install_scale compares each file to sha1/sha256 values in manifest.json inside the update file. No code in the middleware update plugin or truenas_install references MANIFEST.sig; GitHub code search of the truenas org finds MANIFEST.sig only in scale-build and the legacy freenas-pkgtools

claim: Installing an update creates a new boot environment dataset <boot-pool>/ROOT/<version>, clones data/home/root/var-log/audit from snapshots of the running environment, unpacks the rootfs with unsquashfs, sets the pool's bootfs to the new dataset and runs update-grub; on any exception it restores the old bootfs and destroys the new dataset

Boot-environment layout: usr, opt and conf datasets are mounted read-only, the BE root dataset is set readonly=on, and @pristine snapshots are taken; data, home, root, var/log and audit are writable and cloned across updates

Rollback is manual: boot.environment.activate runs 'zectl activate <BE>' (from the UI/API or by picking an entry at the GRUB menu). No automatic health-gated fallback was found; GRUB 'recordfail' in 10_truenas_linux only changes graphics mode, as in Debian's stock script. iX describes rollback as reverting 'with a single reboot'
confidence: medium (absence of auto-rollback inferred from code read)

claim: The apps catalog has trains community (487 apps), stable (17), enterprise (4), test (2) and dev (2). Each app has app.yaml (metadata, min_scale_version, run_as_context, capabilities, lib_version plus hash), questions.yaml (UI form), ix_values.yaml and a Jinja templates/docker-compose.yaml rendered through a versioned Python library
Middleware renders app templates with /usr/bin/apps_render_app and runs them with 'docker --config /etc/docker compose -f <rendered files> up/down'

App upgrade: optionally snapshot host paths, stop the app, render the new version, take a ZFS snapshot of the app's ix-volumes dataset named after the old version, then 'compose up --force-recreate'. App rollback re-renders the old version, optionally rolls the ZFS snapshot back and runs compose up. Both are user-triggered; neither is gated on app health
Custom apps: a user-supplied Compose YAML installs as a custom app, and a catalog app can be converted into a custom app (its rendered compose files are merged into one)
Catalog images are pinned by tag plus sha256 digest (e.g. ollama/ollama 0.40.16@sha256:910d0d81…)

TrueCloud Backup uses restic: the build includes a truenas/restic fork, and cloud_backup runs 'restic backup' (for zvols it first takes and clones a ZFS snapshot); TrueCloud requires a Storj iX account and iX is 'not responsible for charges'

Config backup is a tar of the config database plus, optionally, the password secret seed (pwenc); without the seed a restore loses encrypted fields: cloud credentials, SSH keychain entries and Kerberos keytabs are deleted, and SMB passwords must be reset

Identity: a role table in middleware (FULL_ADMIN plus fine-grained READ/WRITE roles) backs API keys and accounts; TrueNAS 26/27 removes the REST API in favour of JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket with SCRAM-SHA-512 for API keys, and upgrading to 26 clears 2FA secrets that use intervals other than 30 or 60 seconds
